headline: Keep watching — and take a few simple falls-prevention steps now
whatWeNoticed: Nothing you've described points to a fall risk that needs attention right now. A little prevention goes a long way at this stage.
whatDeservesAttentionFirst: There's nothing urgent here. The most useful thing is simply to notice if stumbles, unsteadiness, or hazards start to appear.
helpfulObservationsToMonitor: Any new stumbles, near-falls, or moments of unsteadiness
Holding onto furniture or walls while walking
Avoiding stairs or activities they used to do without a second thought
todayThisWeek: Start a simple log of any stumbles or near-falls, even small ones.
Walk through the home together and look for loose rugs, poor lighting, or clutter on walking paths.
Check that their footwear fits well and has good grip.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Waiting for a 'real' fall before doing anything — near-misses are worth noting too.
Assuming occasional stumbles are just a normal part of aging.
Not mentioning a minor stumble to the doctor because 'nothing happened.'

withYourParent: Keep it light: 'I want to help you stay steady on your feet — mind if we look at a few things together?'
Frame it as prevention, not as a sign something is wrong.
withFamily: Let others know you're keeping an eye on this so everyone notices the same things.
Agree on who checks in and how often.

questionsForHealthcareTeam: At the next visit, could you check for anything that might affect their balance or strength?
Are any of their current medications known to affect balance or cause dizziness?
whatMayBeComingNext: Falls risk tends to build gradually — early awareness is what keeps you ahead of it.
If stumbles or hazards start to add up, it may be worth a fuller falls-risk look.
howToPrepare: Keep a running note of any stumbles or near-falls, with dates.
Know who their primary doctor is and how to reach them.
whatThisDoesNotMean: This does not mean your parent is at high risk of falling — it means nothing urgent has come up yet.
It does not mean your concern was unwarranted.
suggestedNextSteps: Revisit the Concern Check if anything changes.
Explore falls-prevention resources for what to watch for.
